matches.title: Gamemode Idea : Endless (Kinda)

matches.title: Fallen solo Farmless & Cowboyless (no economy tower)
matches.snippet: I did fallen without economy. Some people read the title and that's what you're here for, so I'll just get all the screenshots then I'll do the nerd talk where I might complain about things. The text below the screenshot just explains the circumstances of the game, why I used a loadout, stuff like that. Then I'll go in depth about the challenge and what I think it says about the TDS meta in some ways, real nerd things, if you're just here to see the screenshots I don't mind. Would recommend this challenge though, it's pretty fun This was the first attempt, it was a success, although not a surprise to me personally because I'm using Swarmer. A tower that most people might not think is a top tier, but it's the most cost efficient DPS in the entire game so it made perfect sense. This was just to see how possible moneyless fallen was, and yes that's the term I dubbed for this. I also have Gold Minigunner, so again, really cost efficient DPS just for hiddens. I did another Swarmer run later on, and the Swarmer runs were the only runs where I had enough money by the final wave to afford a Commander micro and Medic micro to place some more Swarmers. Here I just barely failed, the king entered with just around 10k health left. matches.title: Fallen mode rework
matches.snippet: Hello, Fallen mode rework. Fallen mode needs a rework because the gamemode has too many filler waves, and the gamemode is excessively boring due to the lack of enemies that pose a significant challenge. Having too many fillers waves isn't good for the game because the game can get repetitive and boring. The fallen mode rework aims to create strategic options and reduce filler waves to an understandable degree while also increasing the gamemode's overall difficulty. The rewards has been increased in this fallen mode rework. Normal mode and molten mode rework https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000199781 https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/440000000000020251 New wave cash bonus (200+(75 x number of waves completed)/the number of players Ability Cooldown Now shows how long enemies with Non-Passive/Hp Activation Abilities. Some have a different cooldown than other abilities. (No more cooldown rng range). There will be enemies that will be able to boost how frequently enemies use their abilities in future game modes concepts. Defense rework Enemies can get more than 100% defense. Damage reduction can be more than 50%. The minimum damage would be 1. This rework is to make defense melting more useful. Wave structure Wave 1: 5x Abnormal Commander: Enemies are approaching! matches.title: Swarmer fallen solo | No Accelerator, Ranger, Turret, or Minigunner
matches.snippet: That's right, Executioner is all you need for hidden detection, and while the triumph screen does hide the one in the top left corner, I only needed three maxed Executioners, and I guess a max Medic too, but it contributed basically nothing for damage. Executioner was my early game after tanking first 4 waves, although I'm pretty confident you can place it sooner and be fine in terms of farming for level 4 by wave 13. Why the Executioner is so efficient is because of the new targeting settings, specifically farthest, although last can also work pretty well on long straight paths if you have towers to cover leaked enemies (including hiddens), and even random can work somewhat well. This works because the Executioner hitting something with an axe only counts as a bounce once it has hit it's intended target at least once, then everything past that will be a bounce, or extra hit on either the target or other enemy, then return to the tower after using up all bounces. The hitbox of the axe is always active from the moment it is thrown though, so by setting the targeting to farthest or last and making sure the tower is placed a bit close to a straight path, you can set it up so it goes for a target pretty far from it where the axe will hit many other enemies while doing so without needing to return. matches.title: My Hard Mode Ducky Strategy :3
matches.snippet: I kinda made my own strategy to beat the Ducky event on hard mode. This strategy was made for random quad matches, not solo matches. If other players block some spots you had to place towers on; just find another spot that is close enough to the original one. LOADOUT: Pursuit Commander Executioner ( (Golden) Pyromancer if you don't have it.) Mortar Ranger STRATEGY: 1: Place down 2 Lv 3 Executioners. 2: Place down 5 Lv 3 Mortars. 3: Place down 3 Lv 2 Commanders. (Chain Call To Arms.) 4: Place down 5 Lv 3 Pursuits 5: Upgrade the Commanders to Max. 6: Upgrade the Pursuits to Lv 5 (Top path). (DO NOT upgrade to bottom path, because you'll need top path to beat the final boss.) 7: Upgrade the Mortars to Lv 4. 8: Place down 7 Lv 2 Rangers. 9: Upgrade all the Rangers to Max. WAVE 32: Send 2 Pursuits to the right path to take down the problematic Super Soldier Duckys and Ducky Units. FINAL WAVE: Sell your Executioners. Send the Pursuits to the boss when out of range. Upgrade the Mortars to Max (Not Mandatory). Placement Map: Tips; If your teammates are struggling to beat all the Duckys on the right path; send some Pursuits over to them for help. When you've reached the tower placement limit; sell your executioners. And that's how I beat da Hard Mode. My Hard Mode Ducky Strategy :3

matches.title: 750 Solo Molten Strat
matches.snippet: This strat was made for people who are without mini or ranger, high dps towers in general. Molten already is an easy mode but if you are for whatever reason having trouble (such as my friend who I designed this for), use it. Towers: Farm, Ace Pilot, Militant, Military Base, Commander Maps: Harbor, Grassy Isles Waves 1-10 Start with 1 level 2 ace pilot Follow up with a level 2 Militant Proceed to farm if spare time Waves 11-20 Upgrade ace pilot to level 3 and place another at level 3 Upgrade Militant to level 3, place another at level 2/3 If spare time, farm. Waves 21-30 Max Militants and place more. Place another ace pilot, get to level 4/5 Place three commanders for chaining. Get farms to level 4/5. Waves 31-40 Place military bases, all tanks. verified_top_matches.snippet: Forgot about it for a while. The Fallen Invasion is a concept event. It depicts an invasion made by the Fallen Race. It uses enemies from both Fallen and Hardcore Modes even if their names don't have the word 'fallen' in their names. It also features new enemies. You must be level 15 to play the event. You can earn the Battle Pass currency, Crystals, by playing the event, or by playing normal matches. You earn 100 for Normal Mode, 300 for Molten Mode, 500 for Fallen mode, and 1,000 for Hardcore Mode. All rewards are assuming you have triumphed. Unlike previous Battle Passes, rewards always carry over from the previous rank. For example, if you had 342 Crystals in Rank 4, and then earn 853 from a failed Hardcore run, you will have 1195 and then rank up with 595 left over. Would recommend this challenge though, it's pretty fun This was the first attempt, it was a success, although not a surprise to me personally because I'm using Swarmer. A tower that most people might not think is a top tier, but it's the most cost efficient DPS in the entire game so it made perfect sense. This was just to see how possible moneyless fallen was, and yes that's the term I dubbed for this. I also have Gold Minigunner, so again, really cost efficient DPS just for hiddens. I did another Swarmer run later on, and the Swarmer runs were the only runs where I had enough money by the final wave to afford a Commander micro and Medic micro to place some more Swarmers. Here I just barely failed, the king entered with just around 10k health left. This is possibly the best map I could of chosen for this loadout since the crook minions cover the entire map and have surprisingly good range, the Rangers also cover the entire map, and the Crook boss early game spot and Ranger spot is so close I didn't even need to max the rest of the Commanders to reach all of the towers with the ability. The biggest problem was money, I couldn't max all Rangers until the boss had gotten really far onto the track, and the Toxic gunners, while helpful, were not necessary for other enemies. My mindset behind it was it slows everything down by 25% and I can spam it for lots of DPS, but I had so little money to even upgrade my Rangers that I couldn't do that and it didn't work out. Farm is meta for a reason, but fallen actually proves a very fun challenge for me going moneyless, pretty cool. I learned from my mistakes and decided to use Turret. I chose Turret because it has pretty huge map, having covered majority of the track by time it was maxed and there was a max DJ. I barely won though, fallen king was right in front of the exit with a few thousand health when I sold my Turrets to max the rest of them to make sure he died, then I sloppily placed them as you can see there, I only left one in the original Turret spot next to my early game spot. Not much more to say because I plan to talk about the moneyless challenge itself and what makes it challenging in the summary for nerds. This was my most recent win doing moneyless. I did the exact same thing as my first run except I replaced Gold Minigunner with Gold Crook boss instead to see if maybe I would lose to hidden enemies. It went basically exactly the same as last time, except one shadow boss did leak on wave 37 or 38, so I just placed a maxed Gold Crook boss at the end to kill it then moved it back. It leaked because my towers were stunned, and I only had one Medic that was recharging the ability (I couldn't afford a second one and I didn't have the money to just micro one). I also won with this loadout on my first attempt, so I think Swarmer is by far the best tower for this challenge and I'll talk about that a bit more in the nerd summary. Other attempts without screenshots I easily had more than half of my attempts using this one loadout, all of them having failed, and you might be surprised. Commander, DJ, Accelerator, Gold Scout, Medic; for the life of me, I could not get to wave 30 with this loadout, I also tried the same loadout but I replaced Gold Scout with Militant and I still failed. I was playing somewhat casually, if I'm in the mood I can keep trying this loadout, but I just couldn't do it. Gold Scout dominated early game, not much surprise, probably one of, if not the best early game for moneyless, Accelerator itself was the problem. While Accelerator is no doubt one of the best towers in the game at max level, the levels before it aren't really worth it if you think about it. They aren't awful, they can kill and it gets hidden detection completely free, but a Minigunner, gold variant, or even a Militant can get much better damage worth than an Accelerator from the early levels and are still viable at max. I died on wave 27 two times, one because my Accelerator placement wasn't great since I hoped I could max it to cover a good majority of the track on harbor and the Gold Scouts could carry, that did not work. The other loss, which was much more frustrating, was that I placed Accelerator in the perfect early game position on harbor, and that placement also was my downfall on wave 27 because he ended up targeting the slow boss and the glitches killed me again when that's exactly what I was trying to counter.... rough. It uses enemies from both Fallen and Hardcore Modes even if their names don't have the word 'fallen' in their names. It also features new enemies. You must be level 15 to play the event. You can earn the Battle Pass currency, Crystals, by playing the event, or by playing normal matches. You earn 100 for Normal Mode, 300 for Molten Mode, 500 for Fallen mode, and 1,000 for Hardcore Mode. All rewards are assuming you have triumphed. Unlike previous Battle Passes, rewards always carry over from the previous rank. For example, if you had 342 Crystals in Rank 4, and then earn 853 from a failed Hardcore run, you will have 1195 and then rank up with 595 left over. verified_top_matches.title: Solo Molten without Farm or Cowboy.
verified_top_matches.snippet: Okay I just did something crazy today. So I was inspired by the video made by TDS Youtuber: TrustlyDragon, wherein he manages to triumph fallen mode solo without farm or cowboy, so I decided "Heck let's do it!" And surprisingly, I won... I know a valid reason for this triumph: 1.) Golden Crook Boss: Its level 3 upgrade carried early-mid game. 2.) Accelerator: Well uhh it can gain cash from mysteries and a couple of max level accels can handle the Molten Boss. 3.) The boss itself: Literally the boss was weak as heck lol and Molten Mode was easy lol. In my opinion this is a bit tricky but easy to do! If I can do it, then so can you, just make sure you have decent towers. Specifically, the Golden Crook Boss or the Accelerator. It doesn't matter just choose what loadout you wish to choose. Note: No I am not flexing, I'm just sharing something incredibly insane. Proof of triumph: I gave proof... happy? It's surprising how I somehow manage to "speedrun" it, with a time of 15 minutes and 23 seconds. I manage to get 7 Accelerator to max, 1 Commander maxed, and 3 Crook Bosses maxed. The Sledgers were sold for more money. Here is also a picture of my level to prove that I was alone: This is a picture of me as a Level 196 player. (I'm currently 199) Since I'm Level 195+, my base health would be 178. This picture was used during a challenge in the TDS Discord so ignore the weird loadout. H

This works because the Executioner hitting something with an axe only counts as a bounce once it has hit it's intended target at least once, then everything past that will be a bounce, or extra hit on either the target or other enemy, then return to the tower after using up all bounces. The hitbox of the axe is always active from the moment it is thrown though, so by setting the targeting to farthest or last and making sure the tower is placed a bit close to a straight path, you can set it up so it goes for a target pretty far from it where the axe will hit many other enemies while doing so without needing to return. The Swarmers was the typical boss killer with some bee stacking shenanigans, and the Medic I would micro to heal every stun. I used this exact loadout and strategy on Harbor as well and gotten to the final wave, but I died to the king spawning fallens at about the 2nd last turn on the path where the Swarmer's elapsed damage could not kill them in time, something I could of easily solved if I had thought to move the Executioner I had that was out of range, but the boss was brought down to 75k hp. I think it's safe to say that Harbor solo and other shorter maps are definitely going to be possible for Swarmers now as now the Medic will allow them to not lose their stacking setup for each stun, which will cost you the game on a short map. Also possible with Accelerator and Minigunner obviously, probably Turret too. If I win Harbor fallen solo with this loadout I'll post in replies just to prove it. verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: I don't know what to say that's already been said in other posts, so I'll just give general instructions on how the game went and the possible future of a strategy document. A strategy document will obviously have much more detailed instructions than what I'm giving here, but if you wanna try this yourself you will hopefully know what's needed for what waves. P1 loadout: Farm, Swarmer, Gold Soldier, Dj, Medic P2 loadout: Farm, Swarmer, Accelerator, Mortar, Commander Gold soldier for early Mortar on wave 14 Saving for Accelerator and upgrades on wave 19, skipping all waves before level three Level three Dj One maxed Gold soldier Level four Accelerator and one level two Commander in the back (don't need Dj to afford it but p1 can afford it by then) One max Swarmer at front for rushers Maxed Accelerator Then past that you can just freeball it, but I usually get some max Swarmers for money, cta chain, one or two max Accelerators in the middle, then start getting my Mortars. For wave 50: Spam beenades as much as you can until the boss is alone When the boss is alone, all Accelerators are moved to the back with no Dj boost. This guarantees you will survive souls no matter what. Medic micro. My friend used three though because of the difficulty of microing on mobile, but even with the suboptimal dps of a few lost Swarmers it is still a very consistent strategy. All front Swarmers are moved to the back when out of range or almost out of range. Dj is moved to the area in between the middle and back loops when the boss reaches final phase. Recommended to do 4 Commander chain for most of the wave so there isn't any tiny intervals where Swarmers aren't at full stack and so Mortars don't shoot slowly for one cycle. Also since doing a micro would be difficult when you also need to micro Accelerators during the wave, and the boss can spawn plenty of souls so you should have them back there as soon as possible. Recommended that p1 has all Swarmers in front and p2 has all in middle. This is so p1 makes more money as p2's Accelerators will make a lot. We did the opposite in this run, and while p1 still had enough money, the difference in our cash was polarizing. If he was doing a single Medic micro (optimal), then he might of run out of money. This also makes it easy to know where your towers are since the game can glitch out and delete the blue rings under your towers telling you which is yours. Have bait towers at the entrance on the outside angles of the corners up until you see the level 0 Swarmer on the left of the image. Have these out until all of the vindicators are dead or if they all got past the bait towers, but this shouldn't happen. We consistently have gotten past vindicators even when they got circuit boosted each time. Accelerators will handle the first one or two that get circuit boosted. Most Swarmers should be set to strongest. Desyncers (low level Swarmers) should always be set to strongest. Having some max Swarmers set to first is good for strong enemies getting through, like vindicators. Possible strategy document I want to make a strategy document for this since this strategy proved to be very consistent and powerful. I think the instructions for all waves until wave 50 would be pretty simple, and this is practically the highest dps you can get in a duo hardcore game. You can also substitute Mortar for Electroshocker, however it's rng-based for wave 17, so Mortar is more practical for a strategy. I think this strat may actually have a 100% winrate if everything is done correctly, and we didn't even play optimally. We had incredibly bad wave 50 rng for one run and this happened: The screenshot doesn't show it, but we died to him spawning a circuit at the very end because I got lazy and didn't micro my Swarmers at the front, so it was a lot of lost dps. He died just 1 second after he spawned. I also only did a 3 Commander chain for this game. This is why I say that as long as you follow the instructions, even if a bit precise, you should have a very consistent winrate. So even with that horrible rng with so many void slams and spawns, we still had the firepower to kill him and it was due to my laziness that we lost. This is how I might go about making a document: I may do more games with my friend where we switch roles so we both get an idea of what exactly we need to do for each player. Since he doesn't have all of the free time in the world though, after I've got both roles down, I'm thinking some of you can actually participate if you'd like. All that is required for participants is they have Swarmer, and Accelerator if you want to be p2. You don't need to be an active tester or anything, you can play a single game with me just for fun. I want to do this so I can get actual statistics on the winrate of the strategy, counting out player error like messing up early game. verified_top_matches.title: Farm lands fallen solo triumph, but I don't talk about it
verified_top_matches.snippet: Another one. Yes, I forgot to sell the Farms. Not much to say about the solo, but doing these solos is starting to make me think a bit more. I'm starting to think Ranger might actually be better than Accelerator, just maybe. Either way, they make a great team. I need to get more experience with doing solos to truly know, but from my experience so far, the Accelerator is way better for most of the game, but when it comes to the boss wave, my Rangers seem to be a lot better due to the fallen guardians, and their range for attacking the boss as well. I think if the boss didn't have such powerful minions, then the Accelerators would be better due to their insane DPS, even with their range, but that is not the reality we are in, so Rangers seem to dominate for the boss wave. I think I'm still leaning towards Accelerator. It is also very likely just the map though, as Accelerator is best when it has lots of space to utilize, allowing it more time to charge up and allowing it to stay away from the fallen guardians attacks. I like to solo on less optimal maps, which is likely why I'm seeing results with the Ranger, as the Ranger can get more total damage in it's range, but of course it is dealt a lot slower. I also can't forget to mention that it will rarely ever get hit by attacks, and it will also entirely prevent leaking for the most part, although I don't really struggle with that

Now with all of that out of the way, let's see who wins! First up, we have Accelerator. Let's see how he performs, in Solo. First off, early defense will always be Engineer. As both towers are not early game towers. Haha, loser squire- Got a Ranger and Accelerator down at wave 18. Mainly to clean up Fallen Jester and Ranger is there to boost its range. It seems to be 21.85 as of level 3 being boosted. And I must say, this range sucks... No seriously, do you not see how small that covers the first path? It's not that great, and it doesn't seem good for the Golden Minigunner once it's his turn. Regardless, at least it reaches the front. Level 3 Accelerator has a range of 19. I did Accelerator first to test out how big the range is. And it doesn't seem that versatile for that area. For Accelerator, it'll get better when it's maxed. But I'll have to think about it with the Golden Minigunner. Now, for the next level. Now THIS is much better to work with. Almost reaches the entrance and is almost basically full map range with the Ranger's range boost. Not bad, not bad at all. Continuing on with absolute domination. Oh boy, Fallen Tank. Let's see how well you fair against my Accelerators! Oh... So... Sad... And pathetic. Nothing is safe. And I mean it. This was Fallen Summoner before he met the heat death of the universe. And this was Fallen Summoner after meeting the infinite vessel of destruction for three seconds. Rip bozo. Moving on, Fallen Honor Guard came in. Then lost, half of his health by literally existing and getting beamed first. How sad. More random captures. If you're wondering what that is, that's a Fallen Summoner. As for wave 39, it wasn't hard at all. (Of course it isn't.) I just didn't get a capture of destroying it. Now, before getting to wave 40, I'll summarize what Accelerator has done. Most of the waves get spawnkilled instantly with Accelerator. Even wave 39 gets spawnkilled before Fallen Guardians spawned. Accelerator's role as a sub DPS is pretty huge, I kinda recommend it if you need a sweeper. Is it the best? Well, we'll have to see until the end. Now for wave 40, also known as the final wave. We're greeted with a Fallen Shield straight into my face. How cool. And then the Fallen Honor Guard. And then a swarm of Fallen Angels. And lastly, the Fallen King himself. I tried to get a good fudging capture. But I couldn't, because Engineer and Accelerator keep spawncamping EVERYTHING! Doesn't matter. This is good enough. Very good enough. Oh yes! So, he got destroyed. He is not happy. He died on the first turn. No seriously, it's the first turn. As in, the first turn he does on the path of the map... You get what I mean... So with that, Accelerator performed very well for a tower with an eight placement limit. Now, let's move on to our next challenger! The Golden Minigunner. It is time. First off, we know it's Engineer that defends early. But before we move straight to the Minigunner. I got a visual bug? Floating phantom/ghost berries... Anyway. We got the first level 3 Golden Minigunner for wave 18- Oh my goodness, that range is so horrendous... That's like... So terrible from where he is right now... This was quite hard to make him fit. Especially when there's 15 of these guys. Regardless, he isn't Accelerator, so I set him to strongest for Fallen Jester. He did... Decent. Instead of leveling or prioritizing Golden Minigunner like what I did with Accelerator, I upgraded my Engineers instead. It's just because she is the one who has to catch enemies that leak or go to the back. Because the Golden Minigunner can't reach that far... Besides that, I got a Ranger to buff his range. He reaches him, thank goodness for that. After decimating his foes, let's see what's his extra range is next wave. It has to be better! So this is him without the buff. And now, we have- You've got to be kidding me... Well... That's... An improvement?... Okay, I know this look as bad as how level 3 Accelerator was, who was placed farther back. But hey, he's not at his max level, let's not get too hasty on the guy. Now for the max level, we have something better. Yes! He hits the other curve! Too bad bad it only lasts for 20 seconds- At least he has more range towards the entrance. Moving on, more images. The Fallen Tank?! I see that you have returned! Now, are you any better than before? . . . oof... Placed another Golden Minigunner at the back. Is it any good? Well.. It barely reaches the start. But hey, we have the range boost for 20 second

verified_top_matches.title: My Hard Mode Ducky Strategy :3
verified_top_matches.snippet: I kinda made my own strategy to beat the Ducky event on hard mode. This strategy was made for random quad matches, not solo matches. If other players block some spots you had to place towers on; just find another spot that is close enough to the original one. LOADOUT: Pursuit Commander Executioner ( (Golden) Pyromancer if you don't have it.) Mortar Ranger STRATEGY: 1: Place down 2 Lv 3 Executioners. 2: Place down 5 Lv 3 Mortars. 3: Place down 3 Lv 2 Commanders. (Chain Call To Arms.) 4: Place down 5 Lv 3 Pursuits 5: Upgrade the Commanders to Max. 6: Upgrade the Pursuits to Lv 5 (Top path). (DO NOT upgrade to bottom path, because you'll need top path to beat the final boss.) 7: Upgrade the Mortars to Lv 4. 8: Place down 7 Lv 2 Rangers. 9: Upgrade all the Rangers to Max. WAVE 32: Send 2 Pursuits to the right path to take down the problematic Super Soldier Duckys and Ducky Units. FINAL WAVE: Sell your Executioners. Send the Pursuits to the boss when out of range. Upgrade the Mortars to Max (Not Mandatory). Placement Map: Tips; If your teammates are struggling to beat all the Duckys on the right path; send some Pursuits over to them for help. When you've reached the tower placement limit; sell your executioners. And that's how I beat da Hard Mode. My Hard Mode Ducky Strategy :3

verified_top_matches.title: 750 Solo Molten Strat
verified_top_matches.snippet: This strat was made for people who are without mini or ranger, high dps towers in general. Molten already is an easy mode but if you are for whatever reason having trouble (such as my friend who I designed this for), use it. Towers: Farm, Ace Pilot, Militant, Military Base, Commander Maps: Harbor, Grassy Isles Waves 1-10 Start with 1 level 2 ace pilot Follow up with a level 2 Militant Proceed to farm if spare time Waves 11-20 Upgrade ace pilot to level 3 and place another at level 3 Upgrade Militant to level 3, place another at level 2/3 If spare time, farm. Waves 21-30 Max Militants and place more. Place another ace pilot, get to level 4/5 Place three commanders for chaining. Get farms to level 4/5. Waves 31-40 Place military bases, all tanks. Proceed to get 4-6 militants, all max Get all 10 ace pilots, all max. Max commanders If time left, max Military base. While fighting molten boss place more Militants, max level. Your final result should look something like this (aware of the layout, not the win screen) Take into account that I made this strat in an hour and thirty minutes, first 50 to calculate a loadout that would theoretically work and then proceed to test it in the following 40 minutes. Both times successfully worked, so I think it should work. I usually leave farming up to the user, but be aware that they should all be max or level 4 by wave 30. 750 Solo Molten Strat
